To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV patients face many barriers in sustaining employment and re-entering the work force due to their HIV status, their health status and their psychosocial challenges.
HIV patients are concerned about the secrecy of their diagnosis and how this may affect their employment sustainability and re-entry to the workforce.

the main challenges raised in the sustainability of employment among HIV patients in Singapore were: ability to ensure secrecy, ability to secure financial and healthcare resources, ability to ensure stable physical and mental health, ability to cognitatively cope with the concerns of limitations and uncertainty, and ability to work through the challenges of discriminatory practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how HIV patients in Singapore perceive the challenges in sustaining employment, the barriers in workforce re-entry, and the impact of secrecy of the diagnosis on the employment status.
the issues that HIV patients encounter in sustaining their employment.
the ability of HIV patients to sustain their employment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV patients are faced with challenges in sustaining and securing employment.
secrecy of HIV diagnosis, coupled with the individuals' health status and psychosocial challenges, are the key barriers that influence the ability to secure and sustain employment for HIV patients.
secrecy is the most important factor that influences the employment sustainability and re-entry of PLHIV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV patients face multiple challenges in sustaining and securing employment, and that these challenges are compounded by the stigma and discrimination that they face in their workplace.
the ability to sustain employment for HIV patients is dependent upon their ability to manage their health and psychosocial challenges.

the ability to sustain an employment is influenced by a combination of factors that are beyond the control of the individual, and the ability to re-enter the workforce is further compounded by these factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the issue of employment sustainability for HIV patients is not only a medical issue.
the HIV patients are not only concerned about their health but also the ability to maintain their employment and sustain their livelihood.
HIV patients are able to secure and sustain an employment, but the ability to do so is dependent on a number of factors.
